A minimum pair distance of 2^{-h} is encoded by a chain of h intermediate partitions from the indiscrete partition to discrete at level h+1, hence O_{n,h}=2^{binom n2} H_h(n). Conditioning on a refinement layer gives H_{h+1}(n)=sum_{pi in Pi_n} prod_{B in pi}H_h(|B|). Counting strict partition chains and choosing their transition slots gives H_h(n)=sum_{k<=n-1}c_{n,k} binom(h+1,k), whose leading coefficient is (prod_{j=2}^n binom(j,2))/(n-1)!=n!/2^{n-1}. Therefore leading orbit coefficient is n!2^{(n-1)(n-2)/2}. Independently recomputed exact H rows for 1<=n<=7, 0<=h<=3 and leading finite differences through n=5, all matching the claimed table. Special n=1,h=0 cases also follow.
